question: Which two gases are mixed inside an Entonox cylinder?
explanation: Entonox is a 50:50 blend of nitrous oxide and oxygen used for pain relief during labor. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why does Entonox contain 50% oxygen alongside the nitrous oxide?

options.B: To speed up the onset of contractions
options.C: To prevent the mother and baby from lacking oxygen
options.D: To give the gas a pleasant smell

explanation: The high oxygen concentration ensures both the mother and the baby get enough oxygen while using the gas. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h1)

question: What safety feature prevents attaching the wrong gas cylinder to an Entonox regulator?
explanation: The pin-index safety system uses specific pin and hole patterns to ensure only the correct cylinder connects to the equipment. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h2)

question: An Entonox cylinder is stored in a very cold room overnight. What is the main risk if it is used immediately?

options.A: The plastic tubing will melt under high pressure
options.B: The demand valve will stop releasing gas completely
options.C: The cylinder will trigger a fire alarm
options.D: The gases inside may separate and deliver uneven concentrations

explanation: Extreme cold can cause nitrous oxide and oxygen to separate, delivering uneven amounts until the cylinder is warmed and remixed. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h2)

question: When should a laboring woman start breathing in Entonox during a contraction?

options.A: Only when the midwife says the contraction is over
options.B: At the very first sign that a contraction is starting
options.C: Continuously throughout the first stage of labor
options.D: After the contraction has reached its peak

explanation: Inhaling early gives the gas time to enter the bloodstream so it works best when the contraction pain is strongest. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is Entonox considered a self-administered pain relief method?

options.A: The machine senses when the uterus tightens
options.B: The mother holds her own mask and the valve opens only when she breathes in
options.C: The woman adjusts the dosage knob on the machine herself
options.D: The midwife leaves the room so the woman manages the tank alone

explanation: The patient controls the delivery; if she gets too sleepy, her hand drops, stopping the gas and preventing an overdose. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which vital signs are most important to watch in a woman using Entonox?

options.D: Respiratory rate and level of consciousness

explanation: Midwives monitor breathing and alertness to catch early signs of dizziness or excessive sleepiness from the gas. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why is good room ventilation important when Entonox is used often in a labor ward?

options.A: To prevent staff and mothers from breathing in leaked waste gases
options.B: To dry up sweat during the second stage of labor
options.C: To keep the oxygen tanks from overheating
options.D: To ensure the fetal monitor picks up clear signals

explanation: Exhaled nitrous oxide can build up in closed spaces, causing dizziness and fatigue for staff and patients in the unit. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of Entonox during childbirth?

options.A: It puts the mother into a deep sleep during delivery
options.B: It leaves the body very quickly once the mask is removed
options.C: It completely blocks all pain in the lower body
options.D: It requires no breathing technique from the woman

explanation: Nitrous oxide is quickly breathed out through the lungs, so its effects wear off almost immediately after stopping inhalation. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is NOT a typical limitation of Entonox?

options.A: It can cause nausea or lightheadedness
options.B: It provides permanent relief that lasts for days after birth
options.C: It offers only mild to moderate pain relief
options.D: It requires coordinated breathing during contractions

explanation: Entonox wears off within minutes of stopping use and does not provide long-lasting pain relief after birth. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h5)

question: What should a midwife do first if a laboring woman feels dizzy and confused from using Entonox?

options.A: Administer an intravenous sedative right away
options.B: Remove the mask and encourage her to breathe room air
options.C: Position the woman flat on her back without a pillow
options.D: Increase the gas flow rate to maximum pressure

explanation: Taking away the mask allows the nitrous oxide to clear rapidly from the bloodstream, relieving dizziness and confusion quickly. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why might some women experience a dry mouth or mild tingling while using Entonox?

options.A: These are common temporary side effects of breathing the gas mixture
options.B: They mean the blood pressure has risen dangerously
options.C: They show the mother is allergic to oxygen
options.D: They indicate that the baby is in severe distress

explanation: Dryness and tingling are harmless, well-documented side effects of nitrous oxide that disappear quickly after stopping use. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T5#BMP213_U2_T5_h6)
